When asked, your firm stated that it bad not previously heard of the DSCSA. Specifically, (a). Valisure has operated a pharmacy and wholesale distributor business which places them within the DSC SA definition of a trading partner ( dispenser and wholesale distributor) and subjects them to the applicable requirements for those trading partners in the DSCSA. Under the DSCSA, covered product in the possession or control of a wholesale distributor or dispenser which is determined by that person to be a suspect product must be placed into quarantine and not processed further until a determination is made that the product is either cleared or illegitimate. In addition, when a product is determined to be a suspect product, prompt investigations must be conducted in coordination with trading partners, including validating the transaction history and transaction information. There is no documentation demonstrating that your firm appropriately identified products potentially subject to rejection by your laboratory as suspect products in your system(s). Examples include but are not limited to the following products: Bupropion XL lot NB900240 and Metformin lot MTSB19003-A. This Metformin lot was tested in September 2019. When the test results indicated that the lot may be rejected by the Valisure laboratory, your firm decided to reverse distribute the lot. ln these examples, when initial laboratory testing showed that product potentially could be subject to rejection by your laboratory, your firm determined such product to be a suspect product when it concluded there was reason to believe that the product was unfit for distribution. In these situations, and others, your firm failed to coordinate with trading partners and conduct a robust investigation. In addition, your firm has no systems in place for determining and identifying a product as a suspect product in your system(s), and for quarantining and investigating suspect products generally. (b). Your firm could not provide documentation that product rejected by the Valisure laboratory was appropriately identified as illegitimate in your system(s) and that the DSCSA verification requirements were complied with. Examples include but are not limited to the following products: Valsartan lot EVF804A and Metformin lot AMl 80405A. When additional testing by your lab resulted in Valisure's rejection of the lots, the lots at issue were identified as illegitimate because your firm had credible evidence that such product was unfit for distribution. Your firm was then required to make a determination, in coordination with the manufacturer, that the suspect products were illegitimate. Your firm was unable to provide evidence that the lots were appropriately identified as illegitimate in your system or that you sought to coordinate with the manufacturer on making the determination that those products were illegitimate. In addition, there is no documentation demonstrating that your firm has systems in place to identify illegitimate product in your system(s), and for quarantining and dispositioning illegitimate products generally. Valisure는 약국 및 도매 유통 사업을 운영했으며, 이에 따라 DSC SA에서 정의하는 거래 상대방(조제자 및 도매 유통업자)에 해당하고 DSCSA의 해당 거래 상대방 요건을 적용받는다. DSCSA에 따르면 도매 유통업자 또는 조제자가 보유하거나 관리하는 적용 대상 제품을 의심 제품으로 판단한 경우, 해당 제품을 격리하고 문제가 없거나 불법 제품이라고 판단할 때까지 추가로 처리하지 않아야 한다. 또한 제품이 의심 제품으로 판단되면 거래 이력 및 거래 정보 확인을 포함하여 거래 상대방과 협력해 신속하게 조사해야 한다. 귀사의 시험실에서 거부 대상이 될 가능성이 있는 제품을 귀사의 체계에서 의심 제품으로 적절히 식별했다는 문서가 없다. 예로는 Bupropion XL 로트 NB900240 및 Metformin 로트 MTSB19003-A가 있으나 이에 국한되지 않는다. 이 Metformin 로트는 2019년 9월에 시험했다. 시험 결과 Valisure 시험실에서 해당 로트를 거부할 수 있는 것으로 나타나자 귀사는 해당 로트를 역유통하기로 결정했다. 이 사례들에서 최초 시험실 시험 결과 제품이 귀사 시험실의 거부 대상이 될 가능성이 드러났을 때, 귀사는 해당 제품이 유통에 부적합하다고 믿을 이유가 있다고 결론 내리면서 해당 제품을 의심 제품으로 판단했다. 이러한 상황과 다른 상황에서 귀사는 거래 상대방과 협력하여 철저히 조사하지 않았다. 또한 귀사에는 체계 내에서 제품을 의심 제품으로 판단하고 식별하며, 의심 제품을 전반적으로 격리하고 조사하는 체계가 없다. (b). 귀사는 Valisure 시험실에서 거부한 제품이 귀사의 체계에서 불법 제품으로 적절히 식별되었고 DSCSA 검증 요건을 준수했음을 입증하는 문서를 제공하지 못했다. 예로는 Valsartan 로트 EVF804A 및 Metformin 로트 AMl 80405A가 있으나 이에 국한되지 않는다. 귀사 시험실의 추가 시험 결과 Valisure가 해당 로트를 거부했을 때, 귀사는 해당 제품이 유통에 부적합하다는 신뢰할 만한 증거를 확보했으므로 문제의 로트는 불법 제품으로 식별되었다. 이후 귀사는 제조업체와 협력하여 의심 제품이 불법 제품임을 판단해야 했다. 귀사는 해당 로트가 귀사의 체계에서 불법 제품으로 적절히 식별되었거나 해당 제품의 불법 여부 판단을 위해 제조업체와 협력하려 했다는 증거를 제공하지 못했다. 또한 귀사가 체계 내에서 불법 제품을 식별하고 불법 제품을 전반적으로 격리하고 처분하는 체계를 갖추고 있음을 입증하는 문서가 없다. detail_text: Specifically, A. The firm’s training program does not provide comprehensive trainings to conduct the assigned job responsibilities. The trainings programs do not define the requirements for the on-the-job trainings or the qualifications for technical procedures, including operation/calibration of dissolution apparatus, GC, pH meter, Karl Fisher, etc. The self-conducted, SOP trainings are required for most operations and there are no training assessments conducted to verify the training effectiveness. Firm’s personnel showed insufficient knowledge of the written procedures on the routine operations for the assigned job, resulting in numerous incidences of atypical events. B. There are insufficient trainings provided for observed procedural or practical deficiencies, identified from atypical incident events. Refresher trainings are not always required or provided to all affected personnel, for the root causes identified in the reoccurring atypical events. Repeated atypical events from similar root causes have resulted in numerous aborted HPLC sequence runs. During Jan-Oct 2018, I’ve identified at least 34 repeated Drug Product Manufacturer atypical events, related to insufficient handling of HPLC columns, 19 aborted sequence runs from improper column conditioning and 15 events from poor column performance.
